html:
German philosopher who spent almost his whole life in Königsberg in Prussia, now Kaliningrad in Russia. He is one of the most important thinkers of the Enlightenment.

For years he taught at the local university and was known for his regular habits. Then, in his late fifties, he published the Critique of Pure Reason (1781). He was trying to settle a dispute between those who said knowledge comes from reason and those, like David Hume, who said it comes from experience. His answer was that the mind itself shapes experience, through space, time and cause and effect, so we can know the world only as it appears to us.

In ethics he argued for duty and the categorical imperative: act only on a rule you could want everyone to follow, and treat people always as ends, never only as means. His essay "What is Enlightenment?" (1784) told readers to "dare to know", and Perpetual Peace (1795) imagined a league of free states.

Nearly all later Western philosophy, from Hegel onward, starts from him or argues against him.
sum: German philosopher who spent almost his whole life in Königsberg in Prussia, now Kaliningrad in Russia. He is one of the most important thinkers of the Enlightenment.
